In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of the work-preserving speed-up of parallel matrix computations.
the problem of the best achievable parallel speed-up of computation, given the work of the fastest known sequential algorithm.
the problem of finding the best parallel algorithm for a given problem.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in a wide variety of cases, our approach leads to a significant improvement in the algorithmic performance.
, for the class of problems considered, our approach leads to the fastest known parallel algorithms.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the speed-up achieved by our technique is, in many cases, close to optimal.
the speed-up of the best-known parallel algorithm for a given problem is often significantly larger than the number of processors available.
we have developed a general technique for the speed-up of parallel computations, while preserving the work, and we have shown its efficacy on a variety of matrix problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the speed-ups achievable for a given problem depend on its sequential algorithmic complexity, as well as the parallel algorithmic complexity of the problem.
the speed-up of parallel computation can be substantially improved by a judicious choice of the work-preserving parallel algorithm.
a careful analysis of the structure of a sequential algorithm can be a powerful tool to achieve significant improvements in parallel performance.
